 Ada-Calvo lead governor's race by 1,020 votes in final unofficial results 
 Ron Rocky Coloma | The Guam Daily Post 
 Ron Rocky Coloma

 Republican gubernatorial candidates Tony Ada and E.J. Calvo led the race for governor of Guam by 1,020 votes, while attorney general challenger Phillip Tydingco held a lead over incumbent Douglas Moylan, according to the final unofficial results of Tuesday's general election.
 The Guam Election Commission's results, released at 1:30 a.m. Wednesday, showed Ada and Calvo receiving 15,945 votes, or 51.45%, compared with 14,925 votes, or 48.15%, for Democratic candidates Therese Terlaje and Sabina Perez.
 The Republican ticket's lead came as the final unofficial tally also showed Tydingco ahead in the five-way race for attorney general with 11,583 votes, or 38.29%, compared with Moylan's 10,008 votes, or 33.08%.
 Tydingco's margin over Moylan stood at 1,575 votes.
 Meanwhile, Republicans occupied eight of the top 15 positions in the Guam Legislature race, putting the party in position to hold a narrow majority in the incoming 39th Guam Legislature.
 The results remain unofficial pending certification by the Guam Election Commission.
 Voter turnout exceeds 53% 
 A total of 31,414 ballots were cast in the election, representing 53.11% of Guam's 59,146 registered voters, according to the commission.
 Nine blank ballots were recorded.
 In the gubernatorial contest, 30,994 valid votes were counted, along with 69 overvotes and 351 undervotes.
 An overvote occurs when a voter selects more candidates than permitted in a contest, while an undervote occurs when a voter selects fewer candidates than allowed.
 Limtiaco leads congressional delegate race 
 Democrat Alicia Anne Garrido Limtiaco led Republican incumbent James Moylan in the race for Guam's nonvoting delegate to the U.S. House of Representatives.
 Limtiaco, a former attorney general of Guam, received 15,645 votes, or 51%, compared with Moylan's 14,983 votes, or 48.84%.
 The difference between the two candidates stood at 662 votes, with 49 write-in votes recorded.
 The congressional contest recorded 30,677 valid votes, 79 overvotes, and 658 undervotes.
 Republicans hold narrow advantage in legislative race 
 Republican candidates occupied eight of the top 15 positions in the Guam Legislature race, according to the final unofficial results, potentially giving the party a narrow majority in the 39th Guam Legislature.
 Democratic Sen. Chris Barnett received the highest number of votes among the 30 legislative candidates, with 19,783.
 Fellow Democrat Amanda Shelton followed with 15,835 votes, while Republican Sabrina Salas Matanane placed third with 14,220 votes.
 Republicans Jesse Lujan and Christopher Duenas followed with 13,917 and 13,746 votes, respectively.
 Democrat Telena Nelson received 13,488 votes, followed by Republicans Telo Taitague with 13,330 and Hoa Nguyen with 13,329.
 Democrats William Parkinson, Donna Muna Quinata, and Clynton Ridgell also placed among the top 15, receiving 13,120, 12,670, and 12,595 votes, respectively.
 Republican Vincent Borja received 12,235 votes, followed by fellow Republican Shelly Calvo with 11,428.
 Democrat Kallen Perez placed 14th with 11,203 votes, while Republican Shawn Gumataotao held the final position among the top 15 with 11,031 votes.
 Republican William Castro followed in 16th place with 10,884 votes, leaving a 147-vote difference between the candidates in 15th and 16th place.
 If the standings remain unchanged following certification, Republicans would hold eight seats and Democrats seven in the 15-member Legislature.
 3 candidates lead utilities commission race 
 Simon Sanchez, Michael Troy Limtiaco, and Francis Santos held the top three positions in the race for the Consolidated Commission on Utilities.
 Sanchez received 14,624 votes, or 24.11%, followed by Limtiaco with 13,773 votes, or 22.71%.
 Santos received 12,408 votes, or 20.46%.
 Kenneth Perez placed fourth with 10,369 votes, while Roy Adonay received 9,323 votes.
 Voters were permitted to select up to three candidates in the contest.
 Education board results 
 In the Guam Education Board race, John Taitano II received the most votes, with 14,791, or 32.34% of the votes cast in the contest.
 Ronald McNinch Jr. followed with 12,503 votes, or 27.34%, while Isaiah Aguon received 10,251 votes, or 22.42%.
 Ronald Ayuyu received 8,186 votes, or 17.90%.
 All four candidates were competing in a contest in which voters could select up to four candidates.
 Attorney general race 
 In the attorney general contest, Thomas Fisher placed third with 3,842 votes, or 12.70%, followed by Peter Santos with 3,353 votes, or 11.08%.
 Jordan Pauluhn received 1,448 votes, or 4.79%.
 The race recorded 30,254 valid votes, 178 overvotes, and 982 undervotes.
 The final unofficial results provide a preliminary picture of Guam's next administration, legislative makeup, and other elected offices, with the outcomes remaining subject to the election commission's certification process.
